We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience. Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more. The Opportunity The UCF IT division within University Operations is seeking a highly skilled DevOps Engineer IV to serve as the DevOps and Linux Platform Engineering Lead within UCF IT. This senior technical role is responsible for advancing cloud and Linux platform engineering practices across AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and enterprise Linux environments. The position will lead the design, implementation, automation, security, and operational excellence of cloud infrastructure and platform services that support the university's academic, research, and administrative missions. Engineer and support enterprise Linux platforms across cloud and on-premises environments, including configuration management, patching, automation, troubleshooting, and life cycle management. Design reusable automation solutions, scripts, templates, system images, and operational run-books to improve platform consistency and efficiency. Provide technical leadership for the university's Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environment, including cloud architecture, identity and access management, networking standards, monitoring, and automation. Develop and maintain DevOps, orchestration, and release engineering capabilities across cloud and Linux environments. Design, build, secure, and support containerized application platforms using Docker, including Docker image creation, multi-stage Docker builds, container registries, Docker Compose deployments, container networking, and operational best practices. Implement and maintain automated container build and deployment pipelines, integrating Docker technologies into CI/CD workflows to streamline application delivery and environment consistency. Implement automated deployment pipelines, testing frameworks, security controls, secrets management, and rollback procedures to improve service reliability and resilience. Establish cloud and platform engineering standards, architecture documentation, implementation guides, and operational procedures. Consult with university departments, researchers, developers, and technical teams regarding cloud adoption, application hosting, containerization strategies, automation opportunities, and modernization initiatives. Mentor technical staff in DevOps practices, cloud engineering, Linux administration, Docker technologies, automation, troubleshooting, and operational best practices. Knowledge of cloud computing concepts, infrastructure management, security principles, and operational best practices. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical troubleshooting skills, with the ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience designing, implementing, and administering cloud environments within AWS and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Experience developing and maintaining Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar technologies. Experience building and supporting CI/CD pipelines, DevOps workflows, release engineering processes, and automated deployment solutions. Strong Linux systems administration experience, including configuration management, patching, automation, scripting, and performance tuning. Experience with scripting and automation languages such as Python, Bash, or PowerShell; containerization technologies including Docker; building container images with Docker Build; and deploying and managing multi-container applications using Docker Compose and modern application hosting technologies. Knowledge of cloud security, identity and access management, monitoring, observability, backup and recovery, and disaster recovery practices. Experience supporting large-scale enterprise, higher education, or research computing environments.
